claims.statement: DAC7 places seller-information collection, verification, and financial reporting duties on platform operators, including the total consideration paid or credited to each reportable seller.
The DAC7 directive provides that after specified reminders a platform may close the seller account or withhold consideration until required information is supplied.
The European Commission describes the DSA know-your-trader obligation as requiring marketplaces to verify sellers and display contact information.

contrary_evidence: Marketplace operators are already legally responsible for these controls and may prefer first-party systems or full-service compliance providers.
DAC7 explicitly supplies one hold mechanism, but combining tax, DSA, and product-safety policies into a single payout decision may not be legally or operationally appropriate for every platform.

economics.acquisition_route: A compliance gap assessment and shadow-mode integration through PSP and marketplace consultants before any live hold decision
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year path would require roughly one to two million active seller profiles across several platform verticals, implementation revenue, low review cost, and founder retention of a large equity stake
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-16 hours per week, with legal interpretation approved by external counsel and customer compliance owners
economics.gross_margin_basis: Rules and receipt infrastructure less identity checks, product-data calls, secure review labour, and enterprise support
economics.payback: A marketplace may recover fees through reduced manual review and fewer unsupported holds or releases; these costs need to be measured in shadow mode
economics.pricing: Approximately 1-3 PLN per active seller per month plus 0.05-0.20 PLN per payout decision, with implementation fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Seller evidence expires, regulations and policies change, and every payout produces a recurring decision

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A cross-marketplace library of evidence failure modes, resolution paths, and false-hold outcomes could make policy rollout faster and exceptions more precise
fingerprint.customer: EU mid-market goods, services, rental, and creator marketplaces with many long-tail sellers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell through marketplace payment consultants, platform software vendors, PSP implementation partners, and EU compliance boutiques
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Configurable rules, evidence expiry, reminder tracking, payout-provider webhooks, human-review queue, and downloadable compliance receipts
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The marketplace pays per active seller and per policy decision when a payout is released, held, or escalated with an auditable reason
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A seller payout approaches while required identity, tax-reporting, trader, or product-safety evidence is missing, stale, or contradictory

founder_fit: Policy engines, evidence graphs, and anomaly detection align with data and AI skills
The API model is scalable and avoids personal-brand distribution
Shadow-mode validation allows testing without making live payout decisions initially
risks: False holds can harm sellers and create marketplace liability
Legal rules vary by seller activity and member state
KYC, tax, and marketplace-compliance vendors may already bundle the feature
Handling identity and tax evidence creates significant security obligations

structure.control_point: The machine-readable policy decision and evidence receipt attached to a specific seller payout identifier
structure.critical_dependency: Marketplace counsel and payment operations must delegate policy execution and provide complete identity, tax, product, reminder, and payout events

thesis: Mid-market EU marketplaces could use a policy-decision API that combines seller identity, reminder history, DAC7 fields, trader verification, and product-safety signals to return release, hold, or manual-review decisions for their existing payout provider. Each decision would carry a reproducible compliance receipt, reducing ad hoc spreadsheet holds without the startup taking custody.
title: ReleasePolicy API for Marketplaces
uncertainties: Whether mid-market platforms currently coordinate these checks in one or several systems
Which party bears liability for an erroneous release or hold recommendation
The share of seller payouts requiring manual intervention
Access to product-safety and trader-verification events at decision time
